# Shared status watches: separate rate from work

For a shared status watch, report network requests and process launches separately from in-process/SQL scaling. One HTTP request and one bulk SQLite read per 30 s is constant request count, not constant CPU: live-seat descriptor decoding/splitting, cached-health cloning/serialization and SQL history traversal can still grow with the fleet. A cached health endpoint need not make a status request or per-seat I/O.

Review continuity metadata using data ownership: a same-process successor can copy a route from its already-resolved predecessor without another lookup, status check or process inspection. A shared client built once should retain its timeout/no-redirect policy even on construction failure; an error-preserving client state is cheaper and safer than rebuilding or falling back to defaults.

Proof receipts from #241's final review: full head d3ea172cf60b9c18ab463651006555e6ba8cb4f7; CI run 44235226491; successful Rust job 134569619430, artifact 14396524204; 2494 passed, 6 skipped. All selected launch, gate, timeout, rollover and watch regressions passed. The reviewer's timed live baseline was pre-feature only; do not cite it as deployed feature proof or infer a CPU improvement from it.

**magicWand:** have review dispatch consume the full-SHA `just pr-freeze` receipt, so no packet calls a head frozen before it has checks. For a replacement based on newer main, compare `git range-diff` across the old/new patch series rather than treating every base change in a plain endpoint diff as new feature code.

**difficulties:** initial review head was DIRTY and had no CI, so static review and measurement finished before final grading. The PM then supplied the replacement packet; final publication waited for its successful exact-head CI and FINAL freeze. The transient harness observations are COORD-001 and INS-001 in this seat's buffer; no product changes were made by the reviewer.
